_comment: Modrinth projects shipped with the pack, resolved by tools/publish_pack.py. A slug is the part after modrinth.com/mod/. Per entry: side (client/server/both; default comes from the Modrinth project, shader and resource packs are always client), version (exact version_number; default is the newest for the Minecraft version, and for fabric-api the one in gradle.properties) and filename (a stable file name; used for shader packs so iris.properties keeps pointing at them). Required dependencies of mods are added automatically (except skip_dependencies). The 'why' fields are notes only.

mods.why: rendering engine; Iris and the Sodium add-ons need it
shader support
game logic and server tick optimisation (also the integrated server)
less memory used
skips drawing entities you cannot see; big win in the hub
faster immediate-mode rendering (HUD, text, GUI)
culls more hidden faces and models
lowers FPS when the window is in the background
small render and memory optimisations
extra video options (clouds, animations, fog ...)
tidier video settings screen
zoom key (C)
mod list and mod settings screen
food and saturation preview
faster inventory handling
searchable key bindings screen
shulker box contents in the tooltip
held torches and lava light up their surroundings
3D hats and jacket layers on skins
connected glass and other connected textures

shaderpacks.why: pretty, vanilla-friendly, medium cost; the recommended pack
light on the GPU, for weaker machines

resourcepacks.why: the on-fire overlay no longer fills the screen
grass blocks show their top texture on the sides
